transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Well, I'm here because lately I just... I can't seem to keep my head clear at work. I'll be sitting there and I just completely lose track of what my clients are saying to me. And then with the paperwork, I catch myself rereading the same chart note over and over again without it actually sinking in. 

It's getting really frustrating because I just kind of freeze up on really simple decisions that I used to handle without a second thought. So, yeah, I figured I needed to come in and talk to someone about it.
Have you been feeling sad or down lately?

Um, not really, no. I mean, I wouldn't say I feel sad. I haven't really noticed feeling down or anything like that. It's mostly just... just the frustration with my head not working right when I'm trying to do my job.
Have you been feeling anxious or on edge lately?

No, I don't think so. I mean, I'm not sitting there feeling nervous or panicky or anything like that. 

It's really just the focus issues. I get a little annoyed with myself when I can't process what I'm looking at, but I wouldn't say I've been feeling anxious or on edge.
How long have you been experiencing these focus issues?

It's been about a month now. It started right around the time our clinic lost a few staff members. My schedule got shifted around, so now I'm doing a lot of late-evening coverage, and I've had to take on a heavier load of crisis paperwork. That's when I really started noticing the issues.
Do you ever feel empty or uninterested in things you normally enjoy?

Yeah, actually, I have. My guitar has just been sitting in the corner lately. I keep bailing on soccer and volunteering at the shelter. And even when I try to force myself to do things I usually like, like cooking or going hiking, it just feels like I'm going through the motions. It's like there's no point to it.
Do you feel like you're just going through the motions most of the day?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying, it really does feel like that pretty much the whole day. Even when I try to do my normal stuff—like cooking or hiking, or picking up my guitar—it's all just going through the motions. I just do what I have to do, but it doesn't feel like there's any real point to any of it right now.
Do you feel like you've been having a low mood lately?
I'm not really sure. I haven't noticed feeling sad or down, if that's what you mean by a low mood. It's more just... like I said before, I just feel kind of empty and flat.
Do you still enjoy things when you're actually doing them, even if you don't feel like doing them beforehand?

Not really, no. Like I was saying about cooking or hiking... even when I'm actually doing it, I don't get any enjoyment out of it. It still just feels like I'm going through the motions with no point to it. I think that's why my guitar is just sitting in the corner, and why I keep bailing on soccer and the shelter. The fun just never really kicks in once I'm there.
Have you noticed any changes in your weight recently?

Yeah, um, I have. My pants have actually gotten pretty loose lately. I've been skipping meals, but not really on purpose... it's just that most days, I don't even feel hungry until someone reminds me that I need to eat. So I guess I've lost some weight because of that.
Do you feel pleasure when you're doing things that you used to enjoy?

Like I mentioned a minute ago... no, I really don't. There's just no pleasure in any of it anymore. That's why my guitar has just been sitting in the corner, and why I keep bailing on my soccer games and volunteering at the shelter. Even when I try to force myself to do something I used to like, um, like cooking or going hiking, I don't feel anything good. It just feels like I'm going through the motions with no point to it.
Have you been having thoughts of death or suicide?

I don't have a plan to hurt myself or anything like that. But, um... I do keep having these thoughts, like... like maybe it would just be easier if I didn't wake up in the morning. And honestly, that scares me, because being a therapist, I know exactly what that can mean.
Have you been experiencing these thoughts of not waking up in the morning daily?
Um, no, I wouldn't say it's every single day. It's... I haven't really kept track of the exact days, but it's not a daily thing. Just, you know, often enough that it bothers me when it happens.
How long have you been feeling uninterested in things you normally enjoy?

It's been going on for about a month now. Um, it started right around the time the clinic lost some staff. My schedule got shifted into late-evening coverage, and I've had to take on a lot heavier crisis paperwork. So, yeah, it's been about a month of just... not caring about my usual stuff.
Would you say you've lost a significant amount of weight, like more than 5% of your body weight, over the past month?

I haven't actually weighed myself to know if it's exactly five percent, but... yeah, I've definitely lost some weight. My pants have gotten pretty loose lately. It's just that most days I don't even feel hungry until someone actually reminds me to eat, so I've been skipping meals without really meaning to.
Have you experienced a loss of interest in activities for most of the day, nearly every day?

Yeah, pretty much all day, most days. Like, my guitar has just been sitting in the corner gathering dust. I keep bailing on my weekly soccer games and my shifts volunteering at the animal shelter. And even when I try to do stuff I usually like, like cooking a nice meal or going for a hike, it just feels like I'm going through the motions. There's just no point to it, you know? I just don't get anything out of it anymore.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Um, not really, no. I wouldn't say I feel sad. I'm not really walking around crying or feeling upset or anything like that. It's more just... well, like I mentioned, just that feeling of not caring about much. But I haven't really noticed feeling sad during the day.
Do you feel sad most of the day?

Uh, I think I just mentioned this, but no, not really. I wouldn't say I feel sad most of the day. I'm not crying or feeling down like that. It's really just that flat feeling I was talking about, where I just don't care about much.
Do you think the feeling of not caring about things is present even on the days when you don't have those thoughts about not waking up in the morning?

Uh, wait, I don't actually have thoughts about not waking up in the morning. I'm not really sure where that came from. I don't have thoughts like that at all. It's really just the, um, the not caring about things that I deal with every day. But yeah, I'm not wishing I wouldn't wake up or anything like that.
Do you feel sad, even if it's just a little bit, for most of the day?

I know we keep coming back to this, but honestly, no. Not even a little bit. I really just don't feel sad. It's just that flat feeling I mentioned before, where I just don't care about anything. But sadness just isn't really a part of it for me.
Do you think you would enjoy activities again if something interesting came up

I honestly don't think so. I mean, my guitar has just been sitting in the corner for a while now, and I keep bailing on soccer and my shifts at the shelter. Even when I actually try to force myself to do things I usually like, um, like trying to cook or go hiking, I don't enjoy it. It just feels like I'm going through the motions and there's no point to it. So even if something new or interesting came up, I doubt it would make a difference.
